findings.article_says: The effect of the solution pH of 2–8 and ion strength with different concentrations of NaClO4 (0.001, 0.01, 0.1 and 1.0 M) on the uranium adsorption is shown in Fig. 3.

findings.article_says: Figure 4 presents the effect of the contact time of 5–120 min on the U(VI) sorption by HCF and CF in regard to the kinetics at an initial U(VI) concentration of 10 mg L−1 at pH 3.0 at room temperature.

Paramètres des droites de l'encart, lisibles : pseudo-second ordre y = 0.04x + 0.0792, R2 = 0.9995 ; pseudo-premier ordre y = −0.013x + 0.5079, R2 = 0.7086. findings.extracted: ΔH0 et ΔS0 seulement ; ΔG0 et lnKd absents
findings.article_says: The obtained positive ΔS0 and negative ΔG0 values (Fig. 7 insert) suggest that the adsorption process was spontaneous.
findings.fix: outcomes from_figure "Fig. 7" : ΔG0 = −9.40 (303 K), −10.15 (313 K), −11.70 (323 K), −11.66 (333 K) kJ mol−1 (valeurs imprimées dans l'encart, lisibles) ; lnKd ≈ 3.75, 3.88, 4.06, 4.22 mL g−1 ; droite y = −1619.71x + 9.078. Signaler en doute : avec ΔH0 = 13.47 kJ/mol et ΔS0 = 75.47 J/(mol K), ΔG0(323 K) calculé = −10.91, pas −11.70 (incohérence de l'article, ne pas corriger).

findings.article_says: According to Fig. 8, the U(VI) removal percentage with HCF was 99.11% after the first cycling experiment.
findings.fix: outcomes from_figure "Fig. 8" : R(%) cycles 2, 3, 4 ≈ 95.5, 92, 89 (cycle 1 ≈ 99 et cycle 5 ≈ 88 concordent avec le texte).
